bib.title: Unsupervised Representation Learning with Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks

question: Can architectural constraints make convolutional GANs stable to train, and do the learned discriminator and generator features work as general image representations?
hypothesis: Training GANs and reusing parts of the generator and discriminator as feature extractors yields good image representations.
contributions: A set of architectural constraints (DCGAN) that make convolutional GANs stable to train in most settings
Discriminator features used for classification, competitive with other unsupervised algorithms
Visualisation of filters showing specific filters draw specific objects
Generators show vector arithmetic properties on latent Z

method.summary: A family of convolutional GAN architectures (strided/fractional-strided convs, batchnorm, no FC hidden layers, ReLU/LeakyReLU) trained on LSUN bedrooms, a faces set and ImageNet-1k. The ImageNet-trained discriminator's features feed a linear L2-SVM for CIFAR-10 and SVHN.
method.task: unsupervised representation learning / image generation with GANs

datasets.name: LSUN bedrooms
datasets.size: a little over 3 million training examples
datasets.preprocessing: scaled to [-1,1]; no augmentation; near-duplicates removed (about 275,000) with a 3072-128-3072 denoising dropout ReLU autoencoder on 32x32 center-crops, binarised code as hash

datasets.name: Faces (newly assembled)
datasets.size: 3M images from 10K people scraped; approximately 350,000 face boxes used
datasets.source: web image queries of names from dbpedia, OpenCV face detector

datasets.name: CIFAR-10
datasets.preprocessing: features from ImageNet-trained discriminator, all layers maxpooled to 4x4 grid, 28672-dim vector

datasets.name: SVHN
datasets.size: 1000 uniformly class distributed labelled training examples
datasets.split: 10,000 validation split off the non-extra set

models.name: DCGAN
models.architecture: convolutional GAN; generator projects 100-dim uniform Z, four fractionally-strided convs to 64x64 image, no FC or pooling; discriminator strided convs, flattened last conv into single sigmoid
models.hidden: 512 feature maps in highest discriminator layer

other.batchnorm: all layers except generator output and discriminator input

training.objective: GAN adversarial objective (Goodfellow et al., 2014); not restated
training.epochs: LSUN: samples shown after one epoch and five epochs (Figs 2, 3); convergence length not stated

other.note: mini-batch SGD wording plus Adam; suggested lr 0.001 found too high

other.vector_arithmetic: average Z of three exemplars per concept; noise scale +-0.25 for variants

metrics.name: CIFAR-10 accuracy
metrics.definition: regularised linear L2-SVM on discriminator features

metrics.name: MNIST nearest-neighbour test error on generated conditional samples
metrics.definition: nearest neighbour classifier comparing real data to generated conditional samples

baselines: KNN, TSVM, M1+KNN, M1+TSVM, M1+M2, SWWAE
supervised CNN same architecture (64 random-search trials)
eval.protocol: Single reported runs; no seeds or significance tests stated; no log-likelihood or nearest-neighbour search on training set used for generation quality.

results.claim: DCGAN discriminator features from ImageNet-1k pretraining reach 82.8% on CIFAR-10 with an L2-SVM, beating K-means pipelines but below Exemplar CNN.
results.setup: DCGAN trained on ImageNet-1k, all-layer features max-pooled to 4x4, 28672-dim, linear L2-SVM, CIFAR-10
results.quote: This achieves 82.8% accuracy, out performing all K-means

results.claim: With 1000 SVHN labels the DCGAN + L2-SVM reaches 22.48% test error, state of the art at the time.
A purely supervised CNN of the same architecture gets 28.87% validation error after 64 random-search trials, so the architecture alone does not explain the result.
results.quote: It achieves a signﬁcantly higher 28.87% validation error.
results.note: validation error vs test error for DCGAN, not directly comparable

results.claim: On MNIST a conditional DCGAN reaches 1.48% nearest-neighbour test error at 10M samples, versus 3.1% for real data and 6.28%/5.65% for a GAN baseline.
results.setup: MNIST, 10K validation split, nearest neighbour on generated conditional samples
results.table: Table 3, row DCGAN (ours), column Test Error @10M samples (1.48%); @50K 2.98%

results.claim: Dedup removed approximately 275,000 near duplicates from LSUN bedrooms.
Dropping about 200 window-predictive feature maps in the generator mostly removes windows from generated bedrooms.
results.setup: logistic regression on second highest conv layer features; qualitative result (Fig 6)

results.claim: Averaging Z of three exemplars gives stable vector arithmetic; single samples were unstable.

limits: Authors concede instability: with longer training some filters collapse to a single oscillating mode.
Fine-tuning discriminator features left to future work; DCGAN below Exemplar CNN on CIFAR-10.
Quality evidence is mostly qualitative samples; no log-likelihood or sample-quality metric.
No layer counts, channel widths, step counts or seeds given in text; code not linked.
SVHN comparison mixes DCGAN test error with supervised CNN validation error.

terms.definition: in some recent papers, these are wrongly called deconvolutions

lineage.work: Striving for simplicity: the all convolutional net
lineage.note: strided convs replace pooling; guided backprop

lineage.work: Mikolov et al. word vector arithmetic

figures.caption: DCGAN generator used for LSUN scene modeling.
figures.why: Shows the full generator: 100-d Z projected, four fractionally-strided convs to 64x64.
